description: The page the app loads is served by the Basics server on the loopback interface, so it is a remote origin to Tauri and needs its own capability. It gets exactly the window commands a title bar needs: start dragging, minimize, toggle maximize, close (which hides to the tray) and the maximize state plus resize events to pick the right icon. On top of that, Settings gets the four app commands it actually uses: read and write the desktop settings (start at login, start minimized, close behaviour), pick a vault folder through the native dialog, and open the configured vault folder in the file manager. None of them takes a path from the page: choose_vault only ever writes a folder the owner picked, and open_vault_folder opens the vault the running server reported. No shell, filesystem or opener permission is granted, so even a compromised localhost page cannot run processes, read arbitrary files or open URLs through the app.
